disks.path: PNY → hp-sff-cp → VM101 scsi0 100GiB → Talos .79 sda6 → etcd

assessment.reason: Saving cluster state is much faster after the reboot. Matched disk and CPU measurements do not justify replacing this SSD now.
evidence: Original check: the slowest 1% cutoff for the cluster database (etcd) was 43.8 ms; the worst sampled cutoff was 59.9 ms over 24 hours. Competing demands for the physical machine’s CPU could also cause delays.

September 9 at 22:00 UTC: 99% of etcd disk saves finished within 42.26 ms and 99% of database updates within 60.52 ms. Compare these delays with the physical disk and CPU measurements before blaming a component.
Fresh hardware check 2026-09-09T22:01:42.472617+00:00: built-in health check passed; temperature 33°C; power-on hours 24,616 h.
Disk activity watched for 55 seconds: reads 0.027 MiB/s, writes 0.761 MiB/s, average unfinished requests 0.257; this reflects the apps running then, not the disk’s maximum speed.
September 10, 22:24–22:26 UTC: 4,353 WAL saves, p99 7.86 ms; backend commits p99 12.01 ms. The previous-day median five-minute WAL p99 was 53.2 ms.
The dedicated physical SSD completed 8,796 flushes at 0.916 ms mean, queue 0.165 and 7.24% busy; QEMU flush mean was 1.094 ms. Physical means and etcd p99 measure different operations.
Kernel 7.0.14-16-pve applies the PNY NOLPM power-management workaround. No memory pressure, thermal throttling, failed writes or flushes were observed in the matched check. CPU steal was 5.87%.
assessment.impact: Slow saves can make Kubernetes take longer to accept changes or restart and move apps. If this database becomes unavailable, cluster management can stop working.
options: Keep the updated kernel and the dedicated control-plane disk. A matched busy-period recheck is more useful than an immediate SSD purchase.
Consider separately reviewed control-plane CPU priority 200 versus worker 100, then verify latency and worker impact. This is not applied.
constraints: The cluster-management VM has a 100 GiB disk. Confirm how its data is laid out and how to recover it before moving it.
Do not take one drive from a working duplicate-data pair just to obtain a replacement.
verify: Retain WAL p99 below 10 ms and backend commit p99 below 25 ms under comparable activity; watch CPU scheduling delay separately.
Investigate new media/link errors or sustained latency regression before selecting a replacement. Preserve an off-host etcd backup.
assessment.confidence: Verified current improvement. The new kernel workaround is a plausible contributor, not a proven sole cause.

disks.note: Saving cluster state is much faster after the reboot. Matched disk and CPU measurements do not justify replacing this SSD now.

disks.label: September 10 reinspection
disks.summary: All 24 drives report SMART OK; the SFF control-plane disk is no longer a replacement priority.
evidence: All 14 physical collectors were reachable and all 24 drives reported passing SMART status, including both Shed drives, at 22:29 UTC. SMART does not guarantee future reliability.

SFF at 22:24–22:26 UTC: etcd WAL save p99 7.86 ms; backend commit p99 12.01 ms. Physical SSD flushes averaged 0.916 ms, with queue 0.165 and 7.24% busy. These are different measurements, not interchangeable averages.

The planned reboot loaded kernel 7.0.14-16-pve, which applies the PNY CS900 SATA power-management workaround. It is a plausible contributor to improvement, not proof of the sole cause: reboot and workload changed together.
Plan a compatible 1 TB NVMe for Elite’s data drive, which reports 74% endurance used. This is preventive capacity/endurance work, not an emergency or a 74% failure probability.
Keep working mirrors intact. The current storage proposal fits existing SFF, Elite and Dell data disks; buying a rack of drives is unnecessary for the initial protection tier.
disks.limitations: The per-drive detailed SMART and activity tables retain their September 8/9 capture dates. September 10 collector status is shown separately; this does not refresh every old temperature, counter or VM path.

resources.label: September 10 reinspection
resources.summary: Normal compute capacity is sufficient. Keep the Dell for failure headroom.
evidence: All six Talos nodes were Ready after the planned reboot. Seven-day workload measurements and fresh host/DIMM checks inform the proposed capacity plan; no VM sizes or RAM modules were changed.

SFF, Elite and Dell workers currently reserve 41.75 GiB and 13.95 CPU across active pods, including init-container budgets. They offer 90.55 GiB and 27.85 CPU. SFF+Elite alone offer 61.66 GiB/21.90 CPU, enough in aggregate for normal load but less failure headroom.

SFF control-plane CPU steal fell to 5.87% in the later 120-second sample. CPU priority for that VM is a proposed tuning step, not a deployed change; adding CPU or replacing its SSD is not currently justified.

Shed has exactly two RAM slots, both populated with 16 GB Hynix HMA82GS6DJR8N-XN DDR4 SO-DIMMs: 3200 MT/s rated, currently running at 2667 MT/s. Its whole-guest seven-day p95 memory demand was 2.48 GiB.

The spare 8 GB sticks cannot expand a full two-slot machine. A future swap can give Shed 2×8 GB and move its 2×16 GB to a compatible DDR4 mini PC, leaving the third spare unused. Resize the 25,000 MiB Shed VM before removing RAM.
resources.limitations: The detailed resource/VPA tables below remain September 9 records. New capacity figures and request scope appear in Repair plan. Percentiles cover changing workloads and repairs; they are not load-test ceilings.

spread.label: September 10 reinspection
spread.summary: Protect selected app state with two copies; keep a third wired rebuild destination.
evidence: The storage inventory identified 69 active Longhorn volumes with 1,177 GiB requested and about 238.37 GiB used for one copy. Logical requests do not equal physical bytes currently stored.
A proposed 32-volume tier of original app state and databases uses 27.14 GiB. A second copy adds about 25.82 GiB of current bytes but 414 GiB of scheduled claims. No replica counts were changed.

SFF and Elite can hold the selected pair; Dell retains space to rebuild after either fails. Plan 100 GiB for each full protected-set copy, 64 GiB staging per host, and the existing 10% physical-free floor.

GPU enterprise storage is 71 GiB short of those conservative allowances. Its shared boot NVMe fits with only 35.67 GiB remaining, but shares boot/container work and is not an equivalent replacement for Dell.
Shed is reachable again, but Wi-Fi and attached radios still make it unsuitable as a required shared-storage copy. Coroot Keeper placement and flash-only selectors also need separate review.
spread.limitations: Copy placement is a proposal. Resolve attachment failures, verify backups/restores and review selectors before moving data. Two copies do not fix corrupted data or the single control-plane failure domain.

thrashing.label: September 10 reinspection
thrashing.summary: Temporal and DCGM remain clear of the original disk-thrashing fault.
evidence: The post-reboot Temporal recovery run completed in five seconds with its repaired resource budget.
At 22:29 UTC DCGM was scraping successfully with zero restarts, zero measured refault rate and zero memory-pressure stall rate. Its 1 GiB request and 2 GiB limit remain the repaired settings.
The SFF control-plane follow-up separately measured 4,353 real WAL saves in 120 seconds: p99 7.86 ms, compared with a 53.2 ms median five-minute p99 over the preceding day.
The repair cards and benchmark tables below preserve September 9 verification. They are not freshly repeated maximum-speed tests.
thrashing.limitations: Short normal-workload observations verify the original symptoms were absent; they do not prove every disk path or application is healthy.

argo.label: September 10 reinspection
argo.summary: Matching Git and reporting Ready still do not prove an application can recover.
evidence: At 22:28 UTC Argo reported 95 of 100 applications Healthy. Later application repairs and attachment findings are recorded in App health; no aggregate score is claimed for 22:55.
PR #2350 remains open and unmerged: PostHog Redpanda 8→32 GiB and Perplexica backup permissions are proposed changes, not deployed repairs.
After merge, verify ingestion, set an explicit retention budget, and prove a new Perplexica backup with an isolated restore. A successful sync alone does not complete those checks.
argo.limitations: The application table below remains the September 9 inventory. Use Grafana/Argo for current status; this page is a dated service record.

health.label: September 10 reinspection
health.summary: Redis and Flatnotes repairs are verified; SurfSense PostgreSQL integrity and two attachment faults remain.
evidence: SurfSense Redis was repaired at 22:43 UTC and verified at 22:55: PONG, persistence checks passed, and 33 recent tasks observed. The native checker discarded 11,773 bytes from the bad AOF tail; original files are retained locally and on the NAS.

SurfSense remains in recovery: its PostgreSQL source filesystem has confirmed ext4 corruption, not just a broken backup clone. The 22:47 backup clone failed filesystem checks; the prior 21:49 backup succeeded. PostgreSQL answering queries does not establish filesystem integrity. A native 49 MB database dump completed at 23:01 UTC; isolated restore validation is still pending. Retain it and the last successful backup before repair.
Flatnotes was repaired at 22:38 UTC: health OK and its rebuilt index opens with zero documents. No Markdown notes existed in the inspected data, so this is restored operation—not recovered notes.

Open WebUI and Intercept PostgreSQL still fail attachment: snapshot metadata files are zero bytes and reach EOF, while replica data images remain present. No repair is claimed, and this is not proof of failed physical media or a particular hardware cause.
PostHog capacity and Perplexica permissions are in open PR #2350. Ingestion, retention, a successful new backup and a real isolated restore remain pending merge and verification.
health.limitations: Stop migrations and broad replication while source integrity is unresolved. Successful Redis checks do not certify SurfSense PostgreSQL or its backups. Historical workload/backup tables below retain their September 9 date.

plan.label: September 10 reinspection
plan.summary: Keep the Dell, repair active data faults, and add selective protection before buying another host.
evidence: Completed: Temporal/DCGM resource repairs, SFF post-reboot latency verification, SurfSense Redis repair and Flatnotes index repair. Completed operation is separate from proof of complete data recovery.
Next: preserve and recover SurfSense PostgreSQL, resolve Open WebUI/Intercept attachment metadata, and review PR #2350. Verify application behavior, filesystem integrity and real backup restores.

The initial selective-copy tier needs $0 of new hardware. Elite’s 1 TB compatible NVMe is planned preventive work; a DDR4 tall NUC 13ANH with 32 GB is an optional future Dell replacement, not an immediate purchase.
Retiring Dell now removes the spare wired rebuild destination. The current X399 runbook excludes etcd on the GPU host; enough aggregate RAM does not override that hardware constraint.
plan.limitations: Capacity and hardware choices below are not implemented. Each disk migration, VM resize or replication change needs its own reviewed procedure and acceptance checks.

findings.title: SurfSense PostgreSQL: preserve data, then recover the filesystem
findings.evidence: Source ext4 reports double-free and block-bitmap corruption; a later backup clone fails filesystem checks even though PostgreSQL still answers queries.
findings.action: The native database dump completed at 23:01 UTC; validate an isolated restore and retain the last successful backup. Plan supported offline recovery before migrations or broad copy changes. Redis repair remains separately verified.
findings.verify: A restored database opens and validates, the filesystem is sound, and a fresh backup plus isolated restore succeeds.

findings.title: Open WebUI / Intercept: repair attachment metadata
findings.evidence: Zero-byte Longhorn snapshot metadata causes EOF; data images still exist.
findings.action: Preserve the originals and validate a supported recovery path before changing metadata. No physical-disk replacement diagnosis is established.
findings.verify: Volumes attach and each app reads its intended data; verify fresh backups.

findings.title: PostHog / Perplexica: review PR #2350
findings.evidence: Redpanda’s 8 GiB claim is full; Perplexica backup permissions fail.
findings.action: Review the 32 GiB claim and permissions changes, then verify ingestion, retention and backups after merge.
findings.verify: Queue drains, storage growth is bounded, and an isolated Perplexica restore reads the expected files.

findings.title: Redis / Flatnotes: verify the repaired apps
findings.evidence: Redis persistence and recent tasks passed. Flatnotes index opens with zero documents; no Markdown notes were present.
findings.action: Retain the preserved originals and watch normal operation. Do not add automatic destructive startup repair.
findings.verify: Redis remains usable and a fresh backup can restore; Flatnotes can create and search a new test note.

findings.title: SFF control-plane SSD: keep it
findings.evidence: WAL p99 7.86 ms; physical flush mean 0.916 ms; CPU steal 5.87%.
findings.action: Keep the fixed kernel and isolated disk. Consider reviewed CPU-priority tuning before hardware spending.
findings.verify: Comparable busy intervals retain low save latency and no new I/O errors.

findings.title: Selected app state: two copies with rebuild room
findings.evidence: 32 volumes need about 25.82 GiB more at current usage, with 414 GiB additional scheduled claims.
findings.action: Resolve current faults, verify restores, review flash-selector blockers, and stage selective copies while retaining Dell.
findings.verify: Each selected volume has copies on distinct physical hosts, with surviving rebuild capacity and verified app reads.

findings.title: Elite data SSD: plan a compatible 1 TB NVMe
findings.evidence: 74% endurance used is a wear estimate, not an imminent failure prediction.
findings.action: Confirm interface, physical fit and cooling; migrate the 440 GiB data disk and 10 GiB PDM volume with a reviewed rollback.
findings.verify: Replacement health and capacity pass, data reads correctly, and the old drive remains available until recovery is proven.

findings.title: Backup maintenance and restore proof
findings.evidence: Earlier Kopia index-maintenance warning and failed backups need fresh verification.
findings.action: Recheck current maintenance results and retention, then perform an isolated restore from a real backup.
findings.verify: Warning is understood or cleared, backups stay fresh, and recovered application data validates.

repairs.after: 768 MiB reserved / 1 GiB limit / 240-second deadline. Latest completed 21:55 UTC run succeeded in four seconds.

limitations: 55-second passive sample; no new benchmark or stress load.
Role/path descriptions retain baseline mapping timestamp; physical identities were matched privately where available.
Shed disks are unavailable, not healthy by assumption.
SMART does not certify remaining life or power-loss durability.
SMART null attributes mean not reported, not zero.
Passive I/O is a 55-second workload-dependent observation, not maximum performance or a benchmark.
Concurrent Dell reads and Elite writes were not attributed to a specific workload in this evidence.
Elite unsafe-shutdown increments do not establish when or why they occurred.
NVMe percentage-used is an integer lifetime estimate; 1-to-2 percent crossing does not establish one percent wear in a day.

requestMetricScope: Sum of regular app-container reservations for Pending/Running pods with an assigned node; includes known reservations on unreachable Shed. Excludes init-container maxima and pod overhead, so this is not exact scheduler accounting.

capacityPlan.status: Proposal only · keep Dell for now
capacityPlan.summary: Enough capacity for ordinary operation is not the same as room to survive and rebuild after a host fails.

capacity.name: Keep SFF + Elite + Dell
capacity.note: Current workers; approximately 48.8 GiB request headroom and the third wired rebuild destination.

capacity.name: Retire Dell without replacement
capacity.note: Normal requests fit in aggregate, but less outage room and no third wired-storage destination. Not the current recommendation.

copyTier.note: Two copies of selected original app data and databases; keep rebuildable caches and bulk telemetry selective. No blanket three-copy policy. The 100 GiB allowance does not promise every 424 GiB of claims can fill.

hardware.title: Keep the Dell for now
hardware.detail: Its spare wired failure domain matters more than saving a little idle capacity. Do not retire it before attachment repairs, replica placement and a replacement rebuild destination are proven.

hardware.title: Plan Elite’s 1 TB NVMe
hardware.detail: 74% endurance used calls for preventive planning, not panic. Confirm the NVMe interface, size and cooling; preserve its data and Datacenter Manager volume.

hardware.title: Optional 32 GB DDR4 mini
hardware.detail: A tall NUC 13ANH class is a future replacement candidate. Verify the exact model, NIC and drive layout. A 16 GB machine is not a drop-in replacement for Dell’s 30 GiB VM.

hardware.title: Reuse the Shed RAM correctly
hardware.detail: Two slots: DIMM1 and DIMM3, each 16 GB Hynix HMA82GS6DJR8N-XN, rated 3200 MT/s and running at 2667. First resize the 25,000 MiB VM to a reviewed 8–12 GiB budget; shut down, fit two spare 8 GB sticks, and transfer the two 16 GB modules to a compatible DDR4 mini. Third spare stays unused; its exact specs still need checking.

constraints: Stop before migrations or broad copies: SurfSense PostgreSQL has confirmed source-filesystem corruption, and Open WebUI/Intercept still need attachment-metadata recovery.
No GPU control-plane proposal: the current X399 hardware runbook excludes etcd. The verified GPU VM stays within its existing memory reserve.
The enterprise GPU mirror cannot provide the conservative third-copy workspace; shared boot NVMe is a tighter, less isolated alternative, not equivalent to Dell.
Two copies tolerate one host loss, not corruption, two losses, or loss of the sole control plane. Resolve flash-only selectors and verify actual restores before placement changes.
